subject: Runway scenarios & headroom calc for Acme private GPU pool
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-corp.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private pool sizing — 200k daily active users, burst tolerances

Diego,

Thanks for taking this. We kicked off an internal sizing session and want to baseline what a Redwood private pool would look like for our production traffic. High-level: about 200k DAU, peak window 15 minutes at ~18% of DAU, average request payload ~850 tokens (prompt+response), and median p95 latency target 120ms for short-running requests and 400ms for long-form generations.

Questions we need answered for procurement:
- What sustained QPS and burst QPS do you recommend for a 2x safety runway?
- How much headroom should be reserved for KV cache warmup and model quantization variance?
- Networking: recommended NICs, egress caps, and recommended MTU/segmentation for our on-prem racks (we have 100Gbps fabric available).
- What SLA can Redwood commit to on a Dedicated-private carveout (we expect at least 99.9% during business hours)?

We're trying to align the procurement ask with a clear runway calculation (3, 6, 12 months). Any initial numbers or a quick spreadsheet you can share would help speed internal approvals.

Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Cloud Ops, Acme Cloud

Attachment: traffic_summary_q2.csv (see peak windows section)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private pool sizing — 200k daily active users, burst tolerances

Sanjay — thanks for the detail. Short answer: we can produce a conservative runway spreadsheet, but we need a couple of clarifying inputs to get the numbers reliable:

1) Token distribution: you listed ~850 tokens average. Can you share the distribution (median, 90th, 99th) and an example of shorter vs long-form call mixes? That changes batch efficiency and KV cache effectiveness.
2) Concurrency model: are requests synchronous user-facing calls (blocking) or async (webhook response OK)?
3) Persistence: will KV cache be per-request warm (cold starts common) or sticky across sessions (long-lived prefixes)?

Initial assumptions I'll use for a 2x safety runway:
- Baseline sustained QPS: 1.2k (based on 200k DAU, 18% peak in 15m window => ~24000 requests in 15m -> 26.6 r/s, adjusting for concurrency and bursty client behaviour gives 1.2k sustained across multiple tenants; we'll validate against your traffic CSV)
- Burst headroom: 3x sustained (so plan for 3.6k burst QPS per pool)
- Target per-GPU sustained throughput (conservative): ~70 tokens/sec for the long-form quantized variant, 220 tokens/sec for the short-form micro-optimized variant (these represent typical Llama2-like profiles with mixed precision).
- Warmup/kv: plan 10–15% reserve capacity for prefix warmup in the first 5–10 minutes of a peak window.

I've attached a small starter workbook (acme_runway_calc_v1.xlsx) — it's a working calc with scenario tabs. Marissa and Karthik, please review the throughput multipliers and the NIC/egress buckets — Irene, I want your pick on the MTU/segmentation note for the final doc.

I'll follow up with a refined set of runways (3/6/12 months) after your input.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Technical Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: acme_runway_calc_v1.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private pool sizing — suggested scenario math and notes

Diego / Karthik — I reviewed Sanjay's CSV and sketched three distinct runway scenarios in the attached workbook: conservative, baseline, and aggressive. Notes below (pulling figures into prose for clarity):

- Traffic model: Peak 15m window contains ~22.5k requests in the dataset. If we assume 70% short-form calls (median 180 tokens) and 30% long-form (median 1.8k tokens), effective token/s per request mix is ~650 tokens/request. That lowers the earlier 850 average — I used the per-quantile breakdown to compute GPU work.
- Per-GPU samples: For quantized Llama2-13B optimized for throughput we see ~180k tokens/hour (50 tokens/sec sustained) in our private build. For short-form optimized kernel variant it's ~720k tokens/hour (200 tokens/sec). I put both variants into the calc so procurement can see cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Concurrency and batching: Continuous batching reduces cost if request latency tolerance >120ms. Where customers demand strict 120ms p95 for short operations, we need to provision extra GPUs to avoid batching-induced latency. I added a "latency-safe" multiplier of 1.35 for those slices.
- Warmup & KV: I recommend reserving one warm pool node per 40 active QPS in the first 10 minutes of a peak window. Practically this maps to a 12% warmup reserve for Acme's peak mix.
- Networking: Given your 100Gbps fabric, recommend 2 x 100Gbps NIC per rack for redundancy, and a planned egress cap per cluster of 60Gbps to leave headroom for storage and backup traffic. Use MTU 9000 where supported; jumbo frames cut system CPU and improve throughput for large KV transfers.
- SLA note: 99.9% is achievable for regional private carveouts with a 3-node fault domain and rolling upgrades, but we will need a committed on-call/responder window and a documented evacuation plan for planned maintenance to reach that in contract.

I've annotated the workbook tabs: "assumptions", "3mo_runway", "6mo_runway", "12mo_runway", and included a "notes_networking" image. Key numbers from the baseline tab (rounded):
- Baseline sustained tokens/sec required across pool: 1.05M tokens/sec -> translates to ~1500 short-variant GPUs OR hybrid of 320 short-variant + 820 long-variant GPUs using mixed allocation.
- 2x safety runway target: plan for 30% extra GPUs above baseline (covers node failures and quantization variance).

Karthik, can you sanity-check the token/sec to GPU conversion factors? Irene, confirm MTU + NIC guidance and whether we should call out host-level RSS/flow-steering knobs.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: acme_runway_calc_v1.xlsx; network_topology_v2.png; kv_warmup_plan.md

Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Private pool sizing — proposed commit and next steps

Sanjay — thanks for the patience. We finished a baseline + conservative + aggressive runway and validated the GPU conversion factors with Karthik. Summary (baseline):

- Baseline throughput target (business-hours peak): sustained 1.05M tokens/sec across the private pool, which maps to the hybrid allocation in the attached workbook.
- Recommended initial commit: 520 GPUs (hybrid: 170 short-variant, 350 long-variant) which includes ~30% runway over baseline for failover, warmup, and minor model variance. This maps to an expected burst capacity of ~3.2k QPS under the mix assumptions.
- Networking: plan 2 x 100Gbps NIC per rack, cluster egress cap 60Gbps, MTU 9000 recommended, enable host-level RSS and LRO for high-throughput KV transfers.
- Warmup & caching: reserve a warm pool equal to 12% of capacity for the first 10 minutes of a peak; warm pool replacement policy in kv_warmup_plan.md.
- SLA: Redwood can offer a 99.9% regional uptime SLA for the private carveout with a 72-hour evacuation play and a 2-hour business-hours priority on-call response (contractual). If Acme requires tighter operational windows we'll need an elevated support tier.

Next steps:
1) Sanjay: confirm token distribution median/90/99 and whether you require hard 120ms p95 for >=70% of calls.
2) Acme procurement: if the 520 GPU commit looks OK we can move to commercial terms and map pricing.
3) Redwood infra: we will run a 48-hour soak test with a synthetic replay of your traffic in our staging cluster to validate the warmup reserve and burst absorption.

I've uploaded the final workbook to the shared drive and attached a copy here. I'll also open INF-982 to track the soak test outputs.

If this looks good, let's schedule a 30-minute alignment call with your procurement and infra teams on Thurs or Fri.

— Diego
